whatIsBeingAskedFor: A human looks at every page produced by the central Chromium raster workflow and confirms that what the build says is on the paper is what is on the paper. This build proves ink position from the artifact's own glyphs; it cannot see that a value looks wrong to a reader, overlaps a printed word, or sits on the wrong line of a two-line block.
lookHardestAt: Petition page 1, paragraph 1: the arrest-date trio and the two full-measure charge rules beneath it must all be EMPTY. This is the geometry where the blocked artifacts put a participant's name into an offence.
Petition page 2, paragraph 5: the pardon-grant date trio must be EMPTY. Anything printed there asserts a pardon on a date.

Petition page 2 generally: nothing at all is written on this page. Confirm that is legible as an unfilled page rather than as a broken render — every blank on it is an underscore leader on a line whose glyph widths could not be resolved.
Petition pages 3 and 4: the VERIFICATION jurat and the Certificate of Service must be entirely empty.
Order page 1: the defendant name and case number are written; the arrest-date trio, the charge blanks, the class and the statute blanks must be empty.
Order page 2: the defendant's name inside the decree sentence must read as part of that sentence and must not run into 'should be, and'. The Judge and Date rules must be empty.
Order page 3: the DOB is the only thing written in the identification block.
Both documents, boundary fixture: the long name and the long case number must stay inside their measured rules and must not overprint an adjacent caption.
